subject: Recap + next steps: FinLytics inference cost pressure / quantization trial
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: FinLytics inference cost pressure / quantization trial

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call highlights / pain points (what you told us)
- Token/unit economics are the primary blocker: production token spend is driving >55% of ML infra budget.
- High tail latency during hourly batch jobs and marketing-triggered bursts (affects p95 SLA).
- Current ops surface area (multiple home-grown endpoints) makes consistent rollout/testing slow.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Prod serving: in-house Triton-based endpoints on EC2 (g5 instances) with custom autoscaling.
- Average request = ~32 tokens; typical traffic 500–700 RPS daytime, spikes to ~1.8k RPS during campaigns.

Success criteria (what success looks like to you)
- Reduce per-request cost by ~50–70% while keeping p95 < 200ms for 90% of traffic.
- Ability to run canary A/B tests and compare output quality across quantized model variants.
- Clear telemetry / token accounting exported to Redshift for month-over-month TCO comparisons.

Technical notes from the call (what we think matters)
- Batching expectations: you want batch sizes up to ~64 for peak throughput but low-latency paths for single requests.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache could save significant tokens for your recurring prompts (we saw examples where 20–30% of tokens could be cached).
- Quantization openness: you indicated your ML team is willing to try int8 (and per-layer) quantization as long as we validate output quality on a holdout set.

Attachments: attaching a short mutual action plan draft that includes the trial scope and telemetry checklist (mutual_action_plan-draft.pdf).

Proposed next steps
1) You share a small sample of production traces + 1-2 representative prompts (we discussed sample_traces.jsonl).
2) Redwood provides a short TCO sketch and a few model + quantization configurations we recommend for your traffic pattern.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical deep dive next week with Tom (ML infra) to align on traces/ingestion and a 60-min exec sync to agree rollout milestones.

Would Monday 10–10:30am PT for the deep dive work for Tom? If not, send two slots that work.

Thanks — looking forward to running a small proof-of-value that shows unit economics improvement.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

On Wed, May 20, 2026 at 4:10 PM Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:
> ...

Thanks Aditya — this is a helpful summary. Confirming and adding a few clarifications from our end: 

1) Primary pain: token cost and unpredictable spend during promotion-driven bursts (we see cost blowouts when campaigns run). Tail latency impacts customer-facing pages and needs to be addressed in any rollout.

2) Stack details: we run Triton on g5.12xlarge today but have a mix of older g4 instances for lower-priority models. Autoscaling is reactive via CloudWatch + custom lambda.

3) Traffic profile (more detail): baseline 500–700 RPS, burst 1.8k RPS for ~10–15 mins when push campaigns trigger. Average request 28–36 tokens; top 5% of requests are long context (400–600 tokens).

4) Quantization: our ML lead (Tom) is open to int8 and mixed-precision, but we need to define quality gates (token-level match rate, top-k agreement, and a small human review on 200 samples).

5) What we can share now: attaching the RFP doc and a compressed sample trace export (finlytics-rfp-q2.pdf, sample_traces.jsonl). Procurement is on copy to start the contract/terms conversation.

Ask from you: please send a short TCO sketch and two possible trial configurations we can A/B (one higher-precision, one aggressive quantized config) before the technical deep dive — we want this to feed into our internal scoping.

Monday 10am PT works for Tom — thanks.

—Sarah
Sarah Liu
Head of Platform Engineering
FinLytics
sarah.liu@finlytics.com

Attachments: finlytics-rfp-q2.pdf (RFP), sample_traces.jsonl (compressed traces)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Recap + next steps: FinLytics inference cost pressure / quantization trial

Marissa / Vivek — forwarding Sarah's reply and attachments. Key items: they want a TCO sketch + two trial configs before the deep dive, and Tom confirmed Monday 10am PT for the tech sync.

Why this looks promising:
- They have clear cost targets (50–70% reduction) and are open to int8/mixed precision trials.
- Traffic profile (short requests but big spikes) maps well to Redwood's mixed low-latency + batch paths + prefix caching.

Suggested immediate actions (my plan)
1) I will draft a one-page TCO sketch showing per-100k-token unit economics under three modes (hosted default, int8 quantized, cached + batching) — aim to share by EOD Fri.
2) Engineering: propose we run a short pre-demo bench (on a representative trace) with two configs: a) FP16 + conservative batching, b) int8 + aggressive batching + prefix cache. I need help from infra to size and estimate cost.
3) Marissa — can you approve a small trial credit and access to a Redwood staging pool so we can run the bench with their sample_traces? Estimate: ~12–18 hours of GPU runtime to get meaningful numbers.

Attachments included in thread: mutual_action_plan-draft.pdf, finlytics-rfp-q2.pdf, sample_traces.jsonl

If you want, I can also draft a short SOW (1 page) to attach to procurement.

Thanks — Aditya
